Subject: Dedicated cluster sizing: workload cartography + sample trace

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the time today. To get a reliable Dedicated sizing for Nova Labs we need a compact ‘workload cartography’ from your side so our pre-sales sizing can produce a recommended GPU footprint and an autoscale/burst strategy that meets your latency SLOs and cost objectives.

I've attached a short worksheet (workload_cartography_template.xlsx) with the fields below — what would be most helpful is a filled copy + a small traffic sample (CSV) that matches a 24–72 hour slice:

- Primary endpoints (intent labels) and % of traffic per endpoint
- Request type: stateless vs. session/pinned KV cache
- Average prompt tokens and response tokens (tokens per request) — tokenization uses standard BPE estimates
- Typical and peak QPS (1m/5m/15m windows) and estimated concurrent sessions
- Burst characteristics: duration, amplification factor (how much QPS increases compared to baseline)
- Models in use or desired (full name + quantization if known)
- SLO targets (p50/p95/p99 latency for inference), and any hard p99 SLA
- Payload size limits and average input payload (KB) — important for network egress planning
- Any multi-stage pipelines (reranking, embeddings, or external tool calls) and their ordering
- Security constraints: VPC, private peering, SOC2/ISO needs, data residency, KMS/HSM requirements

If you can send the sheet + a small sample (even 1000 rows) it will let us run a lightweight simulator and a rough KV/batching hypothesis.

Proposed next steps:
1) You fill the sheet and attach a 24–72h sample (CSV) — I can accept a sanitized dump.
2) We'll run a quick simulation and give you a 1st-pass recommended GPU footprint and burst strategy in 48 hours.
3) If that looks good, schedule a 60-min sizing workshop with Karthik to walk the assumptions and trade-offs.

Attachment: workload_cartography_template.xlsx (XLSX)

Thanks — attaching a filled copy of the sheet and a small traffic dump (nova_sample_traffic_dump.csv). Quick answers inline below and in the sheet:

- Primary endpoints: /chat (65%), /summarize (20%), /embed (15%).
- We operate session-pinned conversations for chat (KV cache per session ~ average 8 messages/session). Summarize and embed are stateless.
- Tokens: prompts average 45 tokens for chat, responses 180 tokens; summarizer prompts 80 / responses 120; embed payloads ~10 tokens (we batch 8 docs per request).
- Baseline QPS: 40 qps. Typical concurrency: ~300 concurrent active sessions during working hours.
- Peak bursts: we have marketing-driven campaigns that drive short ~3–5 minute spikes up to 1,000 qps (amplification x25) roughly 1–2 times/week.
- Models: currently experimenting with Llama2-13B quantized (8-bit) for chat; embeddings use a small MLP-based embedder.
- SLOs: target p95 < 300ms, p99 < 600ms for chat generation (these are internal targets; procurement may request stronger).
- Multi-stage: chat -> optional re-ranker (adds ~120ms when invoked, 20% of requests).
- Security: require VPC peering and SOC2. Data residency US only.

I've redacted PII in the CSV. The sample contains a 36-hour slice with timestamps, endpoint, tokens_in, tokens_out, session_id, and observed latency (client-side). There's also a short latency snapshot (latency_snapshot_20280710.json) from our client telemetry.

Thanks for the forward and the sample — I ran a quick pass locally against our simulator and here are high-level takeaways and a 1st-pass sizing hypothesis. Caveat: this is a simulator estimate; we should do a focused workshop and run an on-prem load test for accuracy.

Observations from sample:
- Baseline steady-state (40 qps) with 180 token responses has modest GPU utilization if we use batching + KV cache: ~20–30% avg per-GPU.
- Short bursts to 1,000 qps (3–5m) drive sustained GPU saturation without an explicit burst buffer; headroom needed.
- Session pinning increases memory pressure (KV cache) ~8 messages/session * avg 180 tokens -> KV footprint estimate ~2–3 GiB per active session for 13B in 8-bit quant. With 300 concurrent sessions naive pinning will be large.

1st-pass Dedicated recommendation (NOVA-345):
- Baseline reserved: 6 x NVIDIA A100 80GB-equivalent (or 8 x 40GB equivalent with oversubscription tuning). This provides baseline capacity for steady traffic and moderate bursts with batching.
- Burst buffer: reserve an elastic buffer of 4–6 ephemeral GPUs (burst on top of reserved) to absorb short 1,000 qps spikes. We can implement fast autoscale with warm standby instances to avoid cold-start latency.
- KV strategy: recommend session-shard pool (pin only hot sessions above a heat threshold) + eviction policy. This reduces steady memory needs by ~40% versus naive per-session pinning.
- Batching and micro-batching: use dynamic batching with 40–80 token window to hit high GPU throughput while meeting p95 300ms with target p99 ~600ms. We should cap batching delay < 10ms for chat.
- Re-ranker handling: route re-ranker to a separate smaller pool (1–2 GPUs) to avoid adding tail latency to main generator.

Tail/Latency notes:
- With 8-bit quant and a warmed KV cache, p95 ~250–300ms is achievable on the recommended cluster; p99 will be sensitive to queueing during bursts without the burst buffer.
- Cold KV cache and grafting of large sessions can push p99 to multiple seconds; recommend warm-standby or pre-warm heuristics for known campaign windows.

Operational ask / next steps:
1) Confirm whether Nova is comfortable with the suggested warm-burst model (reserved 6 + ephemeral 4–6).
2) Book a 60-min sizing workshop (Karthik + Jonas + Mina + Nova Ops) — I'll prepare a breakdown of tokens/sec -> GPU need and a costs delta table.
3) If they need a stricter p99 SLA, propose increasing reserved capacity to 10 GPUs or adding an aggressive burst buffer and tighter batching limits.

I'll draft a short one-pager with the simulator inputs and a cost estimate to share with procurement.
